name: Quinn Park
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember trying to schedule the part of care that takes no fixed time.” People around the approach to Seabright Court know Quinn by a small Sunday habit. Quinn likes to watch the beach traffic thin enough for workers going the other way.
voice: I am the social worker who suggested a tidy plan. I want to write companionship down without turning it into a timed chore.
appearance: Quinn has a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones. Look for auburn hair cut square at the nape. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a moss-green cardigan with a narrow brass watch set a little fast. In conversation Quinn folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing.
personality: Quinn has an appetite for a good argument about little things and works hard to keep a serious disagreement from being turned into entertainment.
agenda: To support companionship without billing it as a task.
family: Victor Blair is Quinn’s older cousin. Quinn makes the call. Victor is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *A closing hour*, Victor says, “I have never missed that family's party. I always brought a shirt from the dryer smelling of somebody else's soap.”
connections: Jody Clay. A sustainable family date gives the social worker a better measure of companionship than a timed task.
